documents.instruction: The product boundary, maintained Rust entry point, repository layout, and evidence rules must match the dispatcher, reference contract, generated index, and checked-in files.
Keep the ownership boundary, auditability model, acquisition paths, and legacy-runtime caveat aligned with the Rust source and evidence contract.
Re-execute the build, top-level help, non-writing catalog check, and dry verifier after CLI or schema changes; pasted outputs must remain revision-bound and write behavior must be exact.
Every dispatched Rust command, positional, flag, default, side effect, output category, and specialized exit code must match source; retain the warning that sync-readme-examples ignores arguments.
Every environment variable read by the Rust binary, every documented flag default, external executable dependency, network constant, and local path must match source.
Keep process, data ownership, HTTP/retry, crawl writer, PTY capture, fleet boundary, generated-view, and legacy-cutover descriptions source-true.
The three lanes, ordering, write modes, provenance boundary, and gate semantics must match command implementations and the evidence contract.

Quoted refusals and exit behavior must match source or retained executed output; recovery must preserve evidence and explicitly account for mutations that happen before record index-regeneration failure.
Links, safety labels, and command claims must match the two revision-bound executed walkthroughs and current Rust command behavior.
Re-execute only in a disposable isolated directory after lifecycle changes; preserve actual exit codes, measured visual metadata, gap list, and the post-mutation regeneration behavior.
Re-execute the local-only sequence after gate, verifier, drift, guideline, or corpus changes; never imply upstream freshness from --skip-network.
File roles, lifecycle, schema names, normalization, generated-view status, and catalog invariants must match source.
The field table, asset/provenance vocabulary, completeness floor, add/get/remove behavior, and regeneration caveat must match source.
Status derivation, provenance semantics, completeness floors, measurement/gate/drift distinctions, and write modes must remain exact.
Storage paths, page/state shapes, worker/writer/resume behavior, query JSON, current search-site limitation, and empty-state behavior must match source and executed evidence.
Keep the compact recipe consistent with the full isolated transcript, including non-transactional regeneration failure and explicit reconciliation.
Keep commands local-only, checkpoint counts revision-bound, and claims narrower than the measurements performed.
Schema vocabulary, floors, measurement rules, and completeness semantics must match the maintained Rust implementation rather than removed Python filenames.
Keep attribution, removal, relinking, retained-byte, and drift-handling policy aligned with public corpus behavior and Apache-2.0 repository licensing.
Keep credential recovery guidance compatible with the actual consumers of GitHub, Brama, and Stado access; never embed recovered values.
